title: He held in a sneeze and tore his windpipe 🤧
subject: sneeze
description:
Do you hold in your sneezes? 👇

A man in his 30s pinched his nose and closed his mouth to stop a sneeze while driving. Doctors at Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, Scotland, found a 2-millimeter tear in his windpipe, the first known case of its kind, reported in BMJ Case Reports in December 2023. Not medical advice.

Sources: Misirovs et al., BMJ Case Reports (2023), doi 10.1136/bcr-2023-255633; Live Science (2023); The Courier, Dundee (2023); IFLScience (2023)

scenes.text: Hold in a sneeze, and you can tear your windpipe.
A man in Scotland was driving with hay fever when a sneeze came on.
He pinched his nose and shut his mouth. The pressure in his airway may have hit 20 times normal.
His neck swelled. At Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, doctors heard a crackle under his skin.
A CT scan found a 2-millimeter hole in his windpipe.
It healed in 5 weeks. His doctors now warn against pinching your nose to stop a sneeze.
